holidays.name: National Egg Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble egg in all its forms: scrambled, poached, fried, deviled, or hidden in a breakfast sandwich. Home cooks and diners alike crack open a few in tribute.
holidays.origin: National Egg Day is an unofficial American food observance that has been popularized by food bloggers, egg producers, and social media calendars. It has no single documented founder.
holidays.funFact: A hen needs about 24 to 26 hours to produce a single egg, and egg color depends on the breed of the hen rather than on nutritional value.

holidays.name: World Bicycle Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the simple, affordable, clean, and environmentally friendly bicycle. People mark it with rides, races, and by finally pumping up the flat tires in the garage.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly declared June 3 World Bicycle Day in April 2018 after a campaign led by Professor Leszek Sibilski, recognizing the bicycle's contribution to sustainability and health.
holidays.funFact: The ancestor of the modern bicycle, the 'draisine' or running machine, had no pedals at all. Riders pushed themselves along with their feet, like a big wooden balance bike.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Macaroon Day
holidays.description: A day for coconut and chocolate lovers to enjoy chewy, rich macaroons, the gluten-free cousin of the fancy French macaron. Dunking them in coffee is encouraged.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial American food holiday found on food observance calendars. Macaroons trace back to Italian monasteries and spread across Europe, and they became tied to Jewish Passover traditions because they contain no flour.
holidays.funFact: Macaroon and macaron are different treats. The macaroon is a dense coconut mound, while the macaron is a delicate almond meringue sandwich, and mixing them up can start a friendly argument at any bakery.

holidays.name: World Clubfoot Day
holidays.description: An awareness day that spotlights clubfoot, a common congenital condition that is highly treatable, and encourages access to care for children worldwide.
holidays.origin: The observance falls on June 3, the birthday of Dr. Ignacio Ponseti, who developed the non-surgical Ponseti method for correcting clubfoot in the mid-20th century.
holidays.funFact: The Ponseti method uses gentle manipulation and a series of casts instead of major surgery, and it has transformed treatment for children in dozens of countries.

holidays.name: Repeat Day
holidays.description: A playful, self-referential holiday that invites you to do things twice, repeat yourself, and then repeat yourself again. It is a day to say it again, sing the chorus twice, and re-watch your favorite show.
holidays.origin: Repeat Day is an unofficial quirky observance listed on lighthearted calendars of odd holidays, and it is reportedly also celebrated on June 3 for fun. Its humor lies in its own premise.
holidays.funFact: Repetition is a real memory aid. Psychologists have found that spaced repetition helps people learn and remember information far better than cramming does.
